title: APIs & Requests
intro: Learn the basic ideas of APIs & Requests in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: API
items.text: An API is a defined way for one program to communicate with another program or service.

items.heading: HTTP request
items.text: A web API is commonly accessed by sending an HTTP request to a URL.

items.heading: GET
items.text: GET requests are generally used to retrieve data from a server.

items.heading: POST
items.text: POST requests are commonly used to send data to a server to create or trigger something.

items.heading: Response
items.text: An API response contains a status and often data returned by the server.

items.heading: JSON API data
items.text: Many web APIs send structured data in JSON format because it is compact and easy for programs to parse.

items.heading: requests library
items.text: The requests library provides a convenient Python interface for making HTTP requests.

items.heading: requests.get()
items.text: requests.get(url) sends an HTTP GET request and returns a response object.

items.heading: Status codes
items.text: HTTP status codes describe the result of a request; for example, 200 usually indicates success and 404 indicates not found.

items.heading: Timeouts
items.text: Network requests should use sensible timeouts so a program does not wait forever for a server.

items.heading: API errors
items.text: Good API code checks status and handles connection or response errors instead of assuming every request succeeds.
